picked.t: Danish footwear company shuts Vietnam factory, 1,600 workers lose jobs
picked.body: The closure will affect more than 1,600 workers. Truong Van Phong, deputy head of the Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing and Industrial Zones Authority (Hepza), said Tuesday that ECCO Sko A/S of Denmark, the sole owner of ECCO Vietnam Co., Ltd., had decided to dissolve the company. The company attributed the decision to years of declining market demand, which had resulted in excess production capacity. The factory closure is part of the group's global manufacturing restructuring plan, which aims to consolidate operations at a smaller number of its facilities. Employment contracts for workers not offered continued employment will end on Nov. 30, or earlier if their contracts expire before that date. Some employees will be retained for a few months to assist with the dissolution process. The company has promised to pay all outstanding wages, compensation for unused annual leave, and other amounts owed in accordance with regulations. In addition to statutory severance allowances, it will also pay half a month's base salary for each year of service. Any period of employment shorter than 12 months will be rounded up to one year. Workers will also receive a 13th-month salary proportionate to the time they worked during the year. Those asked to assist with the dissolution will receive an additional bonus equivalent to 50% of one day's base salary for each day worked. ECCO Vietnam has also pledged to complete the confirmation of employees' social insurance contribution records and return relevant documents to them. Phong said the company had not defaulted on social insurance premiums. On Monday afternoon, Hepza, the Ho Chi Minh City Labor Federation, and local authorities met with company officials and told them to fulfill all commitments regarding workers' benefits and facilitate their hiring by other businesses. Phong said at least eight nearby companies had expressed interest in hiring around 1,611 workers as of Monday. He add that Hepza, trade unions, and local authorities would coordinate efforts to put affected employees onto new job opportunities. Phung Thai Quang, deputy chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Labor Federation, said he had instructed industrial zone and company-level trade unions to review employee lists and provide support to those losing their jobs. The city's Trade Union Labor Consultation and Support Center will review the policies announced by ECCO Vietnam, compare them with legal requirements, and monitor their implementation. ECCO is a Danish footwear brand founded in 1963. Its factory in the Bau Bang Industrial Park in former Binh Duong Province began operations in April 2020. The 12-hectare plant cost VND861 billion (US$34 million) and had an annual capacity of 8.1 million footwear products and parts. The dissolution of ECCO Vietnam comes even as recruitment opportunities in the footwear industry remain limited. According to the Ho Chi Minh City Employment Service Center, the garment and textile and footwear sectors had 1,306 vacancies but 2,473 applicants in October.

picked.t: '일감이 없네' 덴마크 신발社 에코, 호치민시 공장 가동중단…직원 1,600여 명 ‘날벼락’
picked.body: 덴마크 신발 브랜드 에코의 베트남 생산법인 에코베트남 공장. (사진=Obayashi Vietnam) 덴마크의 프리미엄 신발 브랜드 에코(ECCO)의 베트남 호치민시 생산공장이 줄어든 일감에 결국 해산을 결정하고, 가동을 중단했다. 사측은 수년째 이어진 수요 감소로 인해 실제 생산량이 생산 능력을 크게 밑도는 상황이 장기화한 것을 해산 결정의 배경으로 밝혔다. 에코는 지난 1963년 덴마크에서 설립된 유명 신발 브랜드로, 호치민시(옛 빈즈엉성) 바우방(Bau Bang)산업단지에 소재한 베트남 공장은 2017년 4월 투자 허가를 받아 2020년 4월부터 본격적인 가동을 시작했다. 공장 부지는 전체 12헥타르로, 생산 용량은 신발 및 부속품 연간 810만 켤레에 달한다. 3일 쯔엉 반 퐁(Truong Van Phong) 호치민시수출가공산업단지관리청(HEPZA·헵자) 부위원장은 “에코베트남의 단독 소유주인 덴마크 에코스코A/S(ECCO Sko A/S)가 베트남 법인 해산을 결정했다”고 밝혔다. 에코베트남의 페트르 밀란(Petr Milan) 법인장은 별도의 통지문을 통해 “11월 2일 오후 2시부터 모든 생산 활동을 중단하고, 해산 절차를 마무리하기 위한 필수 인력만 유지한다”고 밝혔다. 사측은 지난 수년간 시장 수요가 줄어 많은 설비가 가동되지 않는 등 생산 능력이 남아돌았다고 설명했다. 이번 공장 폐쇄는 그룹의 글로벌 생산망 재편 계획의 일부로, 기존 일부 공장에 생산을 집중한다는 계획이다. 이번 공장 폐쇄로 공장에 영향을 받을 직원 수는 1,600여 명에 달하는 것으로 전해졌다. 사측에 따르면, 별도 재계약 제안을 받지 못한 직원들은 이달 말 계약이 종료된다. 모든 직원들은 11월 급여와 법정 퇴직수당에 더해 근속 1년당 월 기본급의 50%(12개월 미만인 경우 1년으로 간주)를 지급받게 될 예정이다. 에코베트남에 재직 중이던 직원들은 올해 실제 근무 기간에 비례해 13월의 급여도 받게 된다. 해산 업무를 담당하는 직원들은 근무일수당 기본급 1일분의 50%를 추가로 지급받게 된다. 퐁 부위원장에 따르면, 현재까지 동사의 사회보험 체납은 없는 것으로 확인됐다. 당국에 따르면 에코베트남 공장 폐쇄로 인해 1,600여 명이 새로운 일자리를 찾고 있으나, 동종 업계 채용이 제한적인 탓에 일자리를 찾는건 쉽지 않아 보인다. 호치민시고용서비스센터에 따르면 10월 섬유·봉제·신발 부문 구직자는 2,473명으로 채용 인원(1,306명)의 2배에 가깝다. 한편, 호치민시노동연맹에 따르면, 2일 기준 현재 신발 업체 8곳이 에코베트남 재직자 고용 승계를 위해 협력을 타진한 상태다. 8개사의 채용 규모는 총 3,330명에 달한다. 노조와 헵자는 근로자들에게 적합한 일자리를 주선하기 위해 상기 업체들과 협력을 지속한다는 방침이다.

picked.t: 덴마크 신발 브랜드 에코, 베트남 공장 폐쇄...근로자 1,600여 명 일자리 잃어
picked.body: 에코 베트남의 바우방 산업단지 생산공장 전경. 에코는 글로벌 생산망 재편을 이유로 베트남 공장 가동을 중단했다. /Obayashivn 제공 (호치민=베트남코리아타임즈) 앨런 리 기자 = 덴마크의 유명 신발 브랜드 에코(ECCO)가 베트남 생산공장 폐쇄를 결정하면서 현지 근로자 1,600여 명이 일자리를 잃게 됐다. 수년간 이어진 시장 수요 감소와 생산능력 과잉이 주요 원인으로 지목됐다. 에코 스코(ECCO Sko A/S)는 자회사인 에코 베트남(ECCO Vietnam Co., Ltd.)을 해산하고 호찌민시 바우방(Bàu Bàng) 산업단지에 위치한 신발 생산공장의 가동을 중단하기로 했다. 공장은 2일 오후 2시부터 생산을 전면 중단했으며, 현재 기업 해산 절차가 진행되고 있다. 에코 측은 최근 수년간 시장 수요가 지속적으로 감소하면서 생산능력이 실제 수요를 크게 웃돌게 됐다고 설명했다. 이번 결정은 글로벌 생산 네트워크를 재편하고 일부 기존 공장에 생산을 집중하기 위한 구조조정의 일환이라는 입장이다. 에코 베트남은 공장 폐쇄로 영향을 받는 근로자들의 고용계약을 오는 11월 30일 종료하거나 계약 만료일이 더 빠른 경우 해당 날짜에 종료할 예정이다. 다만 기업 해산 관련 업무를 지원하는 일부 직원은 수개월간 추가 근무하게 된다. 회사는 근로자들에게 미지급 임금과 미사용 연차수당 등 법정 지급액을 전액 지급하겠다고 밝혔다. 법정 퇴직수당과 별도로 근속연수 1년당 기본급의 절반에 해당하는 추가 지원금도 지급할 계획이다. 근속기간이 1년 미만인 경우에도 1년으로 계산한다. 이와 함께 올해 실제 근무기간에 비례한 13개월 급여(상여금)도 지급하기로 했다. 공장 해산 업무를 지원하는 직원에게는 근무일마다 하루 기본급의 50%에 해당하는 추가 수당을 제공한다. 회사는 사회보험 납부 이력 확인과 관련 서류 반환도 마무리하겠다고 약속했다. 호찌민시 수출가공·산업단지관리위원회(HEPZA)에 따르면 현재까지 회사의 사회보험료 체납은 확인되지 않았다. HEPZA와 노동조합 등 관계 기관은 기업 측에 근로자 보상 약속을 충실히 이행하도록 요구하는 한편, 인근 기업들과 협력해 실직 근로자들의 재취업을 지원하고 있다. 에코는 1963년 덴마크에서 설립된 글로벌 신발 브랜드로, 편안함과 기능성을 강조한 가죽 신발 및 캐주얼 신발 제품으로 잘 알려져 있다. 베트남 공장은 과거 빈즈엉성 바우방 산업단지에 위치하며, 2020년 4월부터 본격적인 생산을 시작했다. 약 12만㎡ 부지에 조성된 이 공장의 총 투자액은 약 8,610억 동(약 3,800만 달러)에 달한다. 연간 생산능력은 신발과 관련 부품을 합쳐 약 810만 개로, 베트남 내 에코의 주요 생산거점 중 하나였다. 이번 공장 폐쇄는 베트남 신발·섬유 산업의 고용 여건에도 부담을 더할 것으로 보인다. 호찌민시 고용서비스센터에 따르면 지난 10월 섬유·의류 및 신발 산업의 구인 수요는 1,306명인 반면, 구직자는 2,473명으로 집계됐다. 기업들의 채용 수요보다 구직자가 많은 상황에서 대규모 공장 폐쇄까지 겹치면서 관련 업종의 구직난이 한층 심화할 가능성이 있다. 한편 HEPZA는 에코 공장 인근 기업들과 협력해 실직 근로자들의 재취업을 지원하고 있다. 2일 기준 최소 8개 기업이 약 1,611명의 근로자 채용에 관심을 보인 것으로 전해졌다.   <저작권자(c) 베트남코리아타임즈, 무단 전재-재배포 금지>

picked.t: Vietnam, Japan's biggest source of foreign workers, struggles to recruit more
picked.body: Recruiters blame a weaker yen and more jobs at home, and many workers are turning to other markets, especially Taiwan, where the wait to depart is shorter. For almost a year, Pham Van Trong, human resources manager at a company that supplies workers to Japan and Taiwan, has traveled to rural and mountainous northern Vietnam twice a month to recruit young people for jobs abroad. Based in An Khanh, Hanoi, the company has sent workers to Japan for more than 10 years in food processing, mechanical engineering, automobiles, machine building, seafood and agriculture, and to Taiwan for electronics work. It asks local Women's Union and Youth Union officials to help find candidates, but they turn up only about 10% of the workers it needs. "The villages are empty of young people because they've moved to the big cities to work in services, drive for ride-hailing apps or take factory jobs. Visit their homes and you only find old people and small children," he said. Japan is one of Vietnam's three traditional labor markets. Vietnamese were the largest group of foreign workers there as of October 2025, according to Japan's labor ministry. At the end of June, 176,865 Vietnamese were in Japan as technical interns, more than any other nationality, and another 176,915 as specified skilled workers, Immigration Services Agency figures show. Japan took nearly 28,500 Vietnamese workers in the first half of this year, the most of any market but down from 35,240 a year earlier, Vietnam's Ministry of Home Affairs data show. By the end of August, Taiwan had pulled ahead, 39,890 to 35,837. Trong's company takes more than 600 job orders a year from Japanese partners on average, but filling them has become very difficult, with its supply of candidates down about 60% from before. A decade ago, seven or eight applicants competed for each order. Now there are two per position, or the company accepts anyone who turns up. Its recruiters post in online groups and split up to search the provinces. The company has also relaxed its selection criteria to fill more places. In food processing and auto parts manufacturing, for example, workers used to need to be at least 1.65 meters tall and physically fit to cope with the work and winter weather. Now candidates who fall just short of the height and weight requirements still pass. The company provides transport and covers extra costs for trainees during preparation. Some candidates interview before the Lunar New Year, or Tet, and leave after the holiday, but quotas still go unfilled. Trong said several factors were behind the falling supply, among them more jobs at home. Unskilled construction workers, for example, can now earn around VND20 million ($770). But the main reason, he said, is the weaker yen. One yen used to fetch VND200-220 and now fetches about VND160-170, so every 10,000 yen ($64) is worth VND400,000-600,000 ($15-23) less once converted. Workers' total incomes are 1.2 to 1.5 times what they were 10 years ago, but what they can save and send home has not kept pace. On total incomes of VND30-40 million ($1,150-1,540) a month, workers used to send home VND20-25 million ($770-960), and their savings still hover around that level. "With the yen sliding and savings not growing, workers will think twice," Trong said. Long waits add to the pressure. A National Statistics Office survey found that the average migrant worker waits about six months between starting preparations and departing. Japan, with its strict requirements, takes about seven months of preparation, compared with about four for other destinations in Asia. The wait can leave workers without income, raising costs and the risk of debt, as more than half borrow to go abroad. "Japanese is also a barrier for unskilled workers, because both the receiving and sending sides demand a high level. But whether it's Japan or any other market, the more of the language you know, the better," he said. Even for Taiwan, a less demanding market than Japan that draws workers because departure takes only one to two months, the company's supply of workers has fallen about 30%. It receives 300-400 electronics orders a year and meets about 60-70% of demand. Kim Thanh, who asked that her real name not be used, handles recruitment at a company that sends workers to Japan. She said its warehousing and food processing orders for this year are nearly filled, but three mechanical engineering orders for eight workers have gone unfilled since the start of the month. Thanh said generational differences in attitudes to work also make recruiting harder. Workers born in the 1980s and 1990s generally don't mind heavy work, while younger people weigh other things. Food processing and warehousing, known as "light work, high pay" jobs, tend to draw young applicants. Mechanical work such as semi-automatic welding or operating cutting machines is grueling, demands high skill and attracts few takers. Each order used to draw three or four applicants per place. picked.t: Hanoi airport records strongest growth among Southeast Asia's 10 busiest in October
picked.body: Singapore Changi is the busiest airport in Southeast Asia in October by serving 3.66 million scheduled departing seats, representing a 1.66% increase in capacity year-on-year. Canadian superstar The Weeknd performed two massive shows at Singapore's National Stadium on Oct. 2 and 3, drawing large crowds of foreign fans and partly contributed to the airport's traffic flow. Photo by AFP Bangkok Suvarnabhumi International Airport ranks second with 3.34 million seats, up 3.9%. The airport suffered severe ground-handling staff shortage due to historic flooding in Thailand's capital city from late September to early October that affected thousands of passenger. Photo by Reuters Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport claimed the third place with 3.29 million scheduled seats, an increase of 3.8% year-on-year. The airport expects more traffic in coming months as Malaysia-based AirBorneo Airways has opened ticket sales for direct flights between Kuching and Jakarta, with services set to begin on Nov. 13, 2026. The airline said in a statement on Oct. 31 that flights to Soekarno-Hatta International Airport would operate three times a week, on Mondays, Fridays and Sundays. Photo by Reuters Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia, the largest in Southeast Asia by area, ranks fourth with seat capacity of 3.22 million, down 5.2% year on year. The airport recently began deploying sniffer dogs in departure and arrival halls, as well as baggage-sorting facilities to strengthen security in both passenger areas and airport operational zones, The Star newspaper reported. The sniffer dogs will be stationed at check-in areas to help detect prohibited items early and identify potential security threats linked to targeted flights, New Straits Times reported. Photo by Reuters Ninoy Aquino International Airport ranks fifth with 2.66 million passengers, marking a 1.6% decrease. Located between the cities of Pasay and Parañaque, about 7 kilometers south of Manila, it serves as the primary gateway for travelers to the country. Photo by Reuters Tan Son Nhat Airport in Ho Chi Minh City ranks sixth with 2.29 million passengers, marking a 6.7% increase. The airport handled over 42.4 million passengers last year, a 6.3% year-on-year increase, including 17.8 million international travelers. In recent years, the airport has upgraded infrastructure and improved service quality. From mid-April, the airport has implemented pre-entry information declarations for international arrivals in an effort to reduce immigration processing time. Photo by Quynh Tran Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi ranked seventh with 1.94 million departing seats, up 14.9% from a year earlier, the fastest growth among the airports listed. The increase came in the same month as Hanoi hosted a two-day concert by South Korean group BigBang. The concerts drew nearly 220,000 visitors to Hanoi, including 68,000 foreigners, generating an estimated VND750 billion (US$29 million) in tourism revenue, according to local authorities. Photo by Giang Huy Thailand's Don Mueang International Airport ranked eighth with 1.56 million departing seats, down 11.2% year on year, the steepest decline among the airports listed. Bangkok's second-largest airport experienced disruptions, flight delays and cancellations in late September and early October due to heavy rain and severe flooding in the city. It started replacing handheld metal-detector checks with manual pat-down searches from Nov. 1, potentially extending security screening times for departing passengers. Photo by Reuters I Gusti Ngurah Rai Airport serving Bali, 13 km south of Denpasar in Tuban, comes in ninth with 1.3 million seats, down 0.9%. As Indonesia's second busiest airport, it acts as a hub for major carriers, offering duty-free shopping, lounges, and close access to Kuta and Jimbaran. Photo by Skytrax Sultan Hasanuddin Airport serving Makassar, the capital of the Indonesian province of South Sulawesi, finishes the top 10 with 960,000 seats, up 4.9% This airport serves as the main gateway to eastern Indonesia and is a major regional aviation hub. It is the largest airport in eastern Indonesia and one of only three international airports in Sulawesi. Photo courtesy of the airport

picked.t: Vietnam needs $300B in annual investment, productivity gains to achieve double-digit growth
picked.body: Such rapid growth is not unprecedented in Asia: Singapore's economy expanded by 12.1% a year from 1967-1973 while South Korea's grew at 10.8% in 1986-1988. For Vietnam, achieving the growth is key to its goal of reaching high-income status by 2045. Achieving the growth target hinges on its ability to mobilize resources, allocate and use such resources efficiently, and boost productivity, according to experts at the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum held last week. Dr. Can Van Luc, a member of the National Financial and Monetary Policy Advisory Council, said an investment-to-GDP ratio of 35-40% was a common trait seen in economies like Singapore, South Korea, and China during their periods of rapid growth. Vietnam needs to keep total investment in the economy at around 40% of GDP, he said. "Given the growth target and this investment ratio, we (the council) estimate that Vietnam needs to mobilize $280-300 billion annually, with the amount increasing by around 14% each year." Public investment, which accounts for 20-22% of the total, could cover up to 30% of the amount needed and so the remaining 70% must come from other sources, including the private sector and foreign investment, he said. He also stressed the need to develop the capital market as the stock and corporate bond markets currently account for just 13-14% of investment, while banks make up 51%. Wanming Du, director of index policy for Asia-Pacific at FTSE Russell, forecast that banks would continue to play an important role, but as the economy grows, financing needs would become increasingly diverse and complex. "That is why a deep and well-functioning capital market is absolutely vital. It also helps strengthen the diversity and resilience of the entire financial system." But investing efficiently is just as important as securing more capital. Major Asian economies posted incremental capital-output ratios (ICORs) of three to four during their periods of rapid growth, with a lower ratio reflecting more efficient use of capital. Vietnam recorded ICORs of above six in the last five years. Luc said Vietnam should aim to lower the ratio to 4.5 by shifting public investment into science and technology, education, and healthcare from the current 80% it allocates to infrastructure. Boosting productivity Vietnam needs to improve productivity at every level, from the public sector and state-owned enterprises to private businesses and foreign-invested companies, according to experts. Mariam J. Sherman, World Bank's division director for Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, said a Vietnamese manufacturing worker currently generates around $6.7 in value added per hour, less than half the level in China. Meanwhile, around 85% of jobs in the export sector involve manufacturing activities such as assembly. Growth in Vietnam's total factor productivity (TFP), which gauges how efficiently an economy turns its inputs into outputs, has virtually stalled since 1990, she said. Denis Depoux, global managing director of Germany-based consultancy Roland Berger, said manufacturing accounts for 36% of Vietnam's GDP. The share reaches almost 80% when manufacturing-related services are included, he said. So the key to TFP growth will involve innovation and modernizing the industrial value chain, he noted. Experts at the AEF 2026 noted that Vietnam has ample opportunities to help it achieve double-digit growth, but executing policies effectively while ensuring that macroeconomic stability is not compromised in pursuit of growth is a challenge. World Bank's Sherman said Vietnam is "at the threshold of its second great transformation," one that "should move firms up the value chain, workers into better jobs, and the State from directing the economy to enabling it."

picked.t: AppotaPay showcases payment solutions for retailers, restaurant chains at VIFS 2026
picked.body: AppotaPay showcased its payment solutions at the Vietnam International Franchise Show (VIFS) 2026, held from Oct. 29 to 31 at the Saigon Exhibition and Convention Center in Ho Chi Minh City. The event brought together domestic and international brands, franchisors, restaurant operators and retail technology providers. AppotaPay also introduced two reports examining purchasing power and consumer spending in Vietnam's retail and food and beverage (F&B) sectors, drawing on official statistics and third-party research to identify trends relevant to business planning for 2027. The retail report said sales of retail goods in Vietnam rose 12.8% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026. An InsightAsia survey of 1,236 consumers aged 18-45 in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City found that 49% considered fast checkout and payment "very important" when choosing a convenience store. The F&B report highlighted a gap between consumer spending intentions and business expansion plans. About 35% of surveyed consumers expected to reduce F&B spending in the second half of 2026, while 52% of surveyed businesses planned to expand. The findings highlighted the importance of monitoring consumer demand and operating costs when planning business expansion. Payment solutions for physical and online businesses At the exhibition, AppotaPay demonstrated services designed to manage transactions across physical stores and online channels. Its SmartPOS terminals accept domestic and international bank cards, e-wallets and QR code payments through a single device. Businesses can use them at checkout counters or restaurant tables, track transactions by store or shift, and manage employee access. The AppotaPay Partner platform provides centralized revenue and transaction monitoring across multiple outlets, along with automated payment reconciliation. For online businesses, the company offers a payment gateway for websites and mobile applications, as well as Payment Link, which allows merchants to collect payments for orders placed through social media and messaging platforms. Other features include automatic payment notifications and virtual accounts that help identify and reconcile incoming bank transfers. AppotaPay also introduced QR Global , a cross-border payment service for businesses serving international visitors. The service supports QR payments through selected banking applications and e-wallets from China, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia. Customers can scan merchants' QR codes using supported applications from their home markets, while merchants receive settlements in Vietnamese dong after automatic currency conversion. Integrated into AppotaPay's SmartPOS and SoftPOS solutions, QR Global provides an additional payment option for retailers, restaurants and hospitality businesses serving international customers. A member of Appota Group, AppotaPay provides payment acceptance, collection, disbursement and transaction management services. The company says it serves more than 600 business customers and supports around 30,000 transaction points nationwide. It is licensed by the State Bank of Vietnam to provide payment intermediary services. In March 2026, AppotaPay received PCI DSS Level 1 certification for the fourth consecutive year, meeting international payment card data security requirements.

picked.t: 베트남, 2027년 뗏(설) 상여금 지급계획 조기 확정 지시…25일까지 통보해야
picked.body: 2026년 뗏(설) 당시 호치민시 벤탄시장 앞에 마련된 광장에서 사람들이 기념사진을 촬영 중인 모습. 베트남 정부가 신년 및 뗏(Tet 설) 상여금 계획을 조기 확정할 것을 기업들에 지시하고 나섰다. 베트남 내무부는 최근 관내 기업의 급여 지급 및 체불 현황과 신년 및 내년 뗏 상여금 지급 계획을 조사해 중앙정부 제출을 전국 34개 성·시 내무국에 지시했다. 내무부가 각 지방 내무국에 하달한 지침에는 지역 노동조합과 협력해 근로자 생활 여건을 파악하고 뗏 연휴 노동쟁의와 파업을 막을 방안을 선제적으로 마련하라는 내용이 담겼다. 내무국 등 관련 기관은 기업과 함께 △근로계약 △임금·상여 규정 △근로자 대상 제도·정책 이행 상황을 점검한다. 기업은 올해 생산·사업 실적을 바탕으로 상여금 계획을 수립하고, 이를 근로자에게 공개해야 한다. 내무부에 따르면, 2026년 병오년(丙午年) 뗏 상여금은 1인당 평균 약 870만 동(337.2달러)으로 전년 대비 13% 증가한 것으로 집계됐다. 이 중 국영기업의 1인당 상여금이 평균 940만 동(364달러)으로 가장 많았고, 외국인직접투자(FDI) 기업이 920만 동(356달러), 민간기업 740만 동(287달러) 순을 나타냈다. 한편, 베트남 정부는 내년인 2027년 정미년(丁未年) 뗏(Tet 설) 연휴를 2월 4일부터 10일까지 7일간으로 확정한 상태다. 이에 따라 베트남의 공무원과 공무직근로자, 국가행정기관 근로자는 규정에 따라 내년 2월 4일부터 8일까지 뗏 전 이틀, 뗏 후 사흘을 포함해 법정 뗏 연휴 닷새를 쉰다. 내년 뗏 연휴는 2월 6~7일이 주말과 겹쳐 2월 9~10일이 대체휴일로 지정되며, 공공 부문 근로자들은 2월 11일부터 정상 업무에 복귀한다. 정부의 연휴 계획은 공공 부문에 적용되는 것으로, 민간기업은 공공 부문 계획과 법정 뗏 연휴 5일을 기준으로 연휴 일정을 자체적으로 수립할 수 있다. 정부에 따르면, 사용자(고용주)는 뗏 전후 △2027년 2월 5~11일 △2월 4~10일 △2월 3~9일 등 3가지 방안 중 하나를 선택해 근로자들의 휴무 기간을 설정할 수 있다.

picked.t: Vietnam posts back-to-back monthly trade surpluses
picked.body: Total import-export turnover in October reached an estimated $122.03 billion, up 3.7% from the previous month and 47.4% year on year, according to the National Statistics Office's socio-economic report released on Tuesday. Exports during the month amounted to $64.67 billion, up 8.7% month-on-month and 51.4% year-on-year, while imports in totaled $57.36 billion, down 1.4% month-on-month but up 43.1% from a year ago. Over the first 10 months of this year, total trade turnover reached $1.01 trillion, up 32.3% year on year, exceeding the $1-trillion mark for the first time. Exports rose 27.5% while imports increased 37.4%, resulting in a trade deficit of $12.07 billion. Exports in the 10-month period amounted to $499.24 billion, with domestic businesses contributing $93.93 billion, up 8.2%, and foreign-invested enterprises $405.31 billion, up 33%. Some 37 export products generated over $1 billion each, accounting for 94.9% of total exports, including eight products that exceeded $10 billion, which made up 73.4%. Processing products dominated exports at $452.74 billion, or 90.7%, followed by agricultural and forestry products at $33.48 billion (6.7%), seafood at $10.36 billion (2.1%), and fuels and minerals at $2.66 billion (0.5%). Imports in the first 10 months were worth $511.31 billion. Production materials accounted for $481.03 billion, or 94.1%, while consumer goods made up the remaining 5.9%. Vietnam posted trade surpluses of $40.84 billion with the EU and $3.42 billion with Japan, up 26.8% and 110.4% from a year ago, respectively. Meanwhile, it recorded deficits of $134.94 billion with China, $48.63 billion with South Korea and $16.93 billion with ASEAN. The Ministry of Industry and Trade plans to accelerate exports, diversify markets and improve compliance capacity, focusing on making better use of signed free trade agreements, expanding into new markets, and strengthening early warnings of trade defence cases, tariff barriers, green standards, traceability and rules of origin. It will also support businesses in improving product quality, developing brands and ensuring supply chain transparency, while promoting official export channels, expanding agricultural quarantine agreements, investing in cold-chain logistics infrastructure, and standardizing growing areas and packing facilities to meet partner markets' requirements.

picked.t: Herbalife supports students in developing community projects
picked.body: Herbalife Vietnam is an official sponsor and content co-creator of the fourth season of "New Generation Students 2026", a reality TV program produced and broadcast by Vietnam Television (VTV3). The company is working with organizers to develop themes and messages that encourage students to explore ideas and turn them into practical projects. Herbalife is also supporting participating teams throughout the competition, promoting balanced nutrition and active lifestyles as part of its message on healthy nutrition for young people. The company is extending its support to the program's first nationwide online competition, which invites students to identify local challenges, propose solutions, and develop projects to address community needs. Participants can strengthen their creativity, teamwork, project management, and problem-solving skills while gaining practical experience in implementing their ideas. Vu Van Thang, general manager of Herbalife Vietnam and Cambodia, said young people play an important role in society and make up a significant proportion of the company's independent members in Vietnam. Programs such as "New Generation Students" give young people opportunities to express their views, test new ideas, and gain practical experience, he said. Exposure to different perspectives and experiences can also help students recognize their strengths, identify areas for improvement, and develop skills for their future careers. Thang encouraged students to take initiative, embrace challenges, and remain open to learning. "Young people should believe in themselves, stay eager to learn, and actively embrace new experiences. Every experience can become a lesson that helps them grow and build a foundation for long-term development," he said. "New Generation Students" is a reality TV program in which university students develop ideas and implement projects intended to benefit their communities. Produced and broadcast by VTV3 since 2023, the program has received sponsorship and content development support from Herbalife Vietnam since its first season. The 2026 season airs at 9:30 p.m. every Saturday on VTV3, starting Oct. 17. This year, the program has also introduced its first nationwide online competition, allowing university students across Vietnam to share local concerns, propose solutions, and develop community initiatives. While the television competition features eight official teams, the online version gives more students an opportunity to participate and contribute ideas. VnExpress is the media and implementation partner for the online competition and has developed the website Sinhvienthehemoi.com . The platform provides information about the program, selection rounds, projects, competing teams, participants, local issues, relevant data, and expert perspectives. Registration for the online competition runs from Oct. 24 to Nov. 24 through the official website.
